question: Which side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs?

options.A: The left side of the heart
options.D: The right side of the heart

explanation: The right side of the heart receives used blood from the body and sends it to the lungs to pick up fresh oxygen. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h1)

question: What makes blood flow from one heart chamber to the next?

options.D: Electrical resistance in the vessel walls

explanation: Blood naturally moves from an area of higher pressure to an area of lower pressure as the heart valves open and close. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h1)

question: What is the resting phase of the cardiac cycle called when the heart chambers fill with blood?
explanation: Diastole is the relaxation period that lets blood flow freely into the heart chambers. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h2)

question: Why is a longer diastolic phase important for heart health?

options.A: It gives the heart muscle time to receive its own blood supply
options.B: It lowers the overall blood pressure inside the systemic arteries
options.C: It gives the electrical conduction system time to completely reset
options.D: It prevents the heart muscle from becoming fatigued too quickly

explanation: The heart muscle gets its blood supply during diastole because contracting ventricles squeeze shut their own tiny blood vessels during systole. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h2)

question: What creates the first heart sound, known as the 'lub'?

options.B: Contraction of the left and right atria
options.D: Opening of the aortic and pulmonary valves

explanation: The sudden snapping shut of the valves between the atria and ventricles at the start of a heartbeat makes the 'lub' sound. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h3)

question: What happens during isovolumetric contraction?

options.A: Ventricles contract with all valves closed, keeping blood volume the same
options.B: Blood flows backward into the atria before the valves manage to lock
options.C: Ventricles relax completely while filling rapidly from the venous system
options.D: Atria empty completely into the ventricles while the semilunar valves open

explanation: During this short phase, the ventricles squeeze to build up pressure, but all valves remain shut so the amount of blood inside does not change yet. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h3)

question: Which two values do you multiply together to find cardiac output?

options.A: Blood pressure and total peripheral resistance

explanation: Cardiac output is how many times the heart beats per minute multiplied by the amount of blood pumped with each beat. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h4)

question: If a healthy adult has a heart rate of 70 beats per minute and a stroke volume of 70 milliliters, what is their resting cardiac output?
explanation: Multiplying 70 beats by 70 milliliters gives 4900 milliliters, which converts to 4.9 liters per minute. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h4)

question: How does more blood returning to the heart affect stroke volume?

options.A: It leaves preload unchanged while altering the afterload of the ventricles
options.B: It increases stretch in the heart muscle, which increases stroke volume
options.C: It stops ventricular filling completely by closing the atrioventricular valves
options.D: It decreases preload, which reduces the stretch and lowers stroke volume

explanation: More blood filling the heart stretches its muscle fibers, making the next pump stronger and pushing out more blood. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h5)

question: What term describes the resistance the ventricles must push against to pump blood out?
explanation: Afterload is the pressure in the blood vessels that the heart has to work against to push blood forward. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h5)

question: Which cranial nerve sends signals that help slow down the heart rate?
explanation: The vagus nerve carries calming nervous system signals that help keep the resting heart rate steady and relaxed. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h6)

question: What is the main job of baroreceptors found in the carotid sinus and aortic arch?

options.A: Filtering waste products out of circulation before blood reaches the brain
options.B: Releasing hormones that directly alter the contractility of ventricular muscle
options.C: Measuring oxygen and carbon dioxide levels directly inside the bloodstream
options.D: Monitoring blood pressure changes and signaling the brain to adjust heart rate

explanation: Baroreceptors act as stretch sensors that notice when blood pressure goes up or down, helping the body keep it in a healthy range. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h6)

question: Why does a pregnant woman's cardiac output increase significantly?

options.A: To fight off potential infections common in the female reproductive tract
options.B: To handle the large increase in circulating blood volume needed for the baby
options.C: To prevent the mother's blood pressure from dropping to dangerous levels
options.D: To compensate for the weakening of the maternal heart valves caused by hormones

explanation: Pregnancy causes blood volume to expand so the placenta gets enough blood, meaning the heart has to pump more each minute. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h7)

question: What condition should a midwife suspect if a pregnant woman has severe high blood pressure and fluid in her lungs late in pregnancy?

options.A: Pre-eclampsia affecting afterload and fluid balance
options.B: Normal physiological expansion of blood volume
options.D: Parasympathetic nervous system stimulation of the heart

explanation: Pre-eclampsia causes tight blood vessels and high resistance, which can overload the heart and cause fluid buildup, requiring urgent care. [learn more](BMP111_U5_T12#BMP111_U5_T12_h7)
